rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Adam’s creation and dialogue with Satan are detailed in al-Baqarah and al-A‘raf, Islahi limits this verse’s explanation to its context.
rows.anchor: I will confine myself to explaining the meaning of this verse with regard to its context only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh deny the Prophet from arrogance, not because they lack a sign; like Satan, they reject Muhammad’s superiority through pride in their own power and authority.
rows.anchor: The real reason of the denial of these people is not that they have not been shown any sign of punishment; their arrogance is the real reason for this denial.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression translated ‘just see’ also carries sarcasm and humiliation; the other expression means that locusts consumed lush crops.
rows.anchor: also connotes sarcasm and humiliation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s enmity toward Adam and his progeny continues until Judgement Day; unbelievers are under Satan’s sway, proving his original claim about Adam’s descendants.
rows.anchor: This enmity of Adam (sws) and his progeny with Satan will continue until the Day of Judgement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants Satan the respite he requested until Judgement Day, but Hell will still punish him commensurately for what he does during that respite.
rows.anchor: the respite demanded by Satan from God until the Day of Judgement was given to him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term for frightening means making someone anxious and worried; sawt here means uproar, commotion, and propaganda.
rows.anchor: make someone anxious and worried

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s wide opportunity to mislead is a warning: believers must remain vigilant to protect their faith from his lures.
rows.anchor: It serves as a caution to them so that they should not take it easy and all those who want to protect their faith from his lures should remain forever vigilant.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan may deploy every form of commotion and propaganda, including print, public, and social media, to divert people from the straight path.
rows.anchor: He can employ the print, public and social media with all their influence to his advantage.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The riders and foot soldiers are literal, encompassing wars enemies of Islam incite to persecute believers, not a metaphor.
rows.anchor: bringing over pedestrians and riders mentioned in the verse is not a metaphor. It is a literal fact.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s partnership in wealth and children is realized by worshippers who dedicate wealth to him, name children after him, or sacrifice them for him.
rows.anchor: They will take out a share for him from their wealth and keep their children’s names after him and even sacrifice them for his pleasure.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s promises deceive people into neglecting their duties, including Arab idolaters’ claim that angels bring them near God and Jews’ claim to be favored children whom Hell will not touch.
rows.anchor: all promises of Satan are fake. These include the notion of the idolaters of Arabia that the angels they worship bring them closer to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reassures the faithful that Satan cannot compel them to stray; God alone has absolute authority and protects servants who trust Him.
rows.anchor: whatever Satan can do, his power is not absolute; he cannot forcibly lead people astray. Absolute authority is with God only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 66–72 depict people invoking God in calamity then returning to arrogance once safe, followed by two groups: those who learn from the world and those who remain blind; Quraysh are first addressed, but all arrogant people fit the pattern.
rows.anchor: The succeeding verses depict the attitude of people when they are caught in some calamity. On such instances, they call upon God and plead before him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable teaches that every favour comes from God and obliges gratitude, yet people credit themselves or alleged deities, call on God alone in calamity, and forget Him once rescued.
rows.anchor: whatever favour people get is actually from God. They can benefit from it and they owe this obligation to it that they are thankful to God for it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enables a ship carrying thousands of tons to cross the sea for people’s benefit; they ignore Him during safe sailing, plead to Him in danger, then forget their distress on shore.
rows.anchor: God has made this possible so that people benefit from their sea travel and be grateful to this favour.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage assures the Prophet that a requested punishment sign will not guide Quraysh: they will pray during calamity, revert to wrongdoing when safe, and a sign cannot guide those who ignore nature and reason.
rows.anchor: he should not think that the Quraysh will accept the path of faith and guidance once he shows them the sign of punishment they are asking.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question warns that God’s dominion is not confined to sea: He can sink people on land or devastate them and their homes with a stone-hurling wind, with no rescuer.
rows.anchor: who can save them from Him?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasif means something that smashes and breaks; tabi means a helper or supporter.
rows.anchor: something which smashes and breaks something

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being spared once does not free people from obligation to God; their ingratitude may bring another punishment, as verse 75 says no one will help against God.
rows.anchor: They think that once they have been let go by God, they have no obligation towards Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human honour and provision should prompt gratitude rather than Satan-like arrogance; human superiority over other species is limited, since other creatures may be superior.
rows.anchor: the honour mentioned in this verse entails that they must remember these favours of God and instead of showing arrogance, be grateful to Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anas means a group of people and imam means leaders or chiefs; at judgement each group is summoned with its pious or impious leaders, and their records go to the right or left hand.
rows.anchor: Every group will be called by God along with its leaders: the pious with their pious leaders and the impious with their impious leaders.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous read their right-hand records gratefully and see no injustice; the left-hand group instead feels frustration and shame at its evil deeds.
rows.anchor: they will happily read every thing and be thankful to God for His graciousness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gathering groups with leaders both honours them and completes proof: righteous leaders see the fruit of risking their lives, while followers of evil curse their leaders and demand double punishment.
rows.anchor: Gathering each group with its leaders and followers has the aspect of honouring them as well as conclusive communication of the truth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those blind to their destination in this world will be raised blind and even farther astray in the next, where return to the straight path is no longer possible.
rows.anchor: Since these people remained blind in this world, they will be raised up blind in the next one as well.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section IX tells the Prophet to hold his position despite demands to amend the Qur’an; rivals may force migration but will then face the messengers’ precedent, while prayer and a pre-migration supplication bring perseverance and victory, and the Qur’an is cure for believers but a scourge to rivals.
rows.anchor: In the succeeding verses, it is emphasized on the Prophet (sws) to adhere to his stance in spite of opposition from his rivals.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording implies opponents tried to make the Prophet abandon his stance through severe trials, but God protected him.
rows.anchor: the opponents of the Prophet (sws) have launched such a massive onslaught against him that by inflicting him with various trials they may well have made him give up his stance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When opponents see preaching take root, they turn from blind opposition to political intrigue or compromise; Quraysh offered amendments to the Qur’an for friendship, and reports name Thaqif, while the Prophet longed for their faith but could not alter revelation.
rows.anchor: Narratives mention the name of the Thaqī f tribe in this regard. This was a very tough phase for the Prophet (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about slight inclination describes the Prophet’s hesitation between unalterable divine directives and his desire for his people’s guidance; God dispelled that reluctance.
rows.anchor: The words “it may well be that you become a little inclined to them” point to his reluctance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic protection from error allows indecision or a passing wrong inclination, provided it is not evil in desire; God protects and redirects a prophet from an incorrect step even along a virtuous path.
rows.anchor: infallibility of prophets does not mean that they can never be in a state of indecision or a wrong inclination cannot pass through their hearts.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The translation presents a conditional warning: if the Prophet inclined to rivals, God would double-punish him in this life and the next, leaving no helper.
rows.anchor: We would have doubly punished you of life and death. Then you would not have found anyone against Us as your helper.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A governing noun is omitted from ‘double the life and death’; the sense is double punishment in this life and the next, proportionate to a messenger’s high rank and accountability.
rows.anchor: This warning of a two fold punishment is according to the rank and status of a messenger.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means to make someone anxious or apprehensive, and al-ard here refers to Makkah.
rows.anchor: to make some anxious and apprehensive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After compromise failed, the opponents intensified their opposition and exerted full force to drive the Prophet from Makkah.
rows.anchor: When the Prophet’s opponents lost hope of any compromise, their opposition, which was no less earlier as well, increased two fold.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger completes proof and seeks forgiveness for his people while present; when they force migration, proof is complete and God either punishes the land or believers’ swords defeat its people—the latter befell Makkah.
rows.anchor: The process of conclusive communication of the truth stands complete. After this, either God’s torments appears and cleanses the land of this filth or the swords of the believers are unleashed on these people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suppressed construction puts God’s established practice toward earlier messengers in focus and emphasizes that it does not change.
rows.anchor: Such suppression emphasizes a certain thing and keeps it under direct focus.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to establish prayer means to be diligent and vigilant in prayer.
rows.anchor: does not merely mean to offer the prayer. It means to show

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duluk is the sun’s descent in three stages—midday, leaving the line of sight, and setting—marking zuhr, asr, and maghrib; lam marks time, conventionally meaning ‘at.’
rows.anchor: There are three stages of this: one, when it descends from midday, second when it descends from the line of sight and third when it disappears from the horizon.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghasaq al-layl means the pronounced darkness at the start of night, the time of isha; Islahi takes the phrase as accusative by specification, emphasizing fajr rather than governing it with ‘establish.’
rows.anchor: darkness of the first part of night when it becomes pronounced

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic ‘recitation’ refers to Qur’an recitation at fajr, generally prolonged and audible; its being witnessed includes attentiveness of imam and followers and angels’ presence, mentioned in a hadith.
rows.anchor: also referring to a prolonged and audible recital of it in general terms.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an itself specifies the five prayer times and, in the next verse, tahajjud’s time; denying this after explicit mention merits a prayer for guidance.
rows.anchor: It is evident from this that the times of the five prayers is mentioned in the Qur’ ān itself.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer times reflect the sun’s standing, kneeling, and prostration, as well as that of things receiving its light; Islahi cites 13:15 and 17:44 for cosmic prostration and glorification.
rows.anchor: It is evident from the verse under discussion that the sun remains in the state of standing, kneeling and prostration in all the times of night and day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation’s posture calls people to pray and join its submission, yet humans bow to trivial things and act proud before their Lord, though those things themselves submit; the sun is a striking example despite being worshipped.
rows.anchor: All these creations of God invite human beings through their form and state that just as they kneel and prostrate before God, people too should do so

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is urged to persist in prayer for patience and perseverance during hardship; divine support is indispensable, and tahajjud is its greatest means.
rows.anchor: the greatest means to seek this support is the prayer, especially the tahajjud prayer, which is discussed in the next verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahajjud literally means rising after sleeping briefly and technically is prayer offered at night after sleep; the pronoun’s bi marks time and refers back to ‘night.’
rows.anchor: to get up after sleeping a little at night

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafilah means an additional favour; laka makes tahajjud obligatory for the Prophet, who maintained it throughout life, as support and strength against satanic opposition.
rows.anchor: It is used in the positive sense always, implying abundance and addition in favours.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though not obligatory for everyone, tahajjud is the strongest means of divine aid for those resisting satanic forces and establishing truth, and righteous religious servants have kept it.
rows.anchor: this prayer is not an obligation for the common man, yet for those who embark upon fighting satanic forces and establishing the rule of truth on earth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When expectation is attributed to God, its hopeful sense belongs to the addressees; this resolves why hope is ascribed to an all-knowing God, and the same applies to la‘alla.
rows.anchor: This interpretation also dispels the notion raised by those not conversant with the language that when everything is known to God, why should hope and expectation be ascribed to him?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqaman mahmuda is a verbal noun in the sense of an emphatic object, not a place noun; the Prophet should hope God raises him to a praised station with a great praising community.
rows.anchor: It is in fact a verbal noun and here it is in the meaning of a stressed object

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qul can mean ‘pray’; sidq means stability and permanence, while sultan means dominance and authority.
rows.anchor: It is used in this meaning in the Qur’ ān at a number of instances.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet faced conditions making migration from Makkah necessary, but messengers do not migrate without God’s permission; this first supplication signals an honourable, secure entry and departure and promised divine help, arranged before departure.
rows.anchor: The fact that the verse first mentions his entry shows that arrangements have been made for it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Especially from Yourself’ promises that God Himself will arrange the Prophet’s aid despite appearances; the supplication is a glad tiding fulfilled in the Prophet’s migration and entry into Madinah.
rows.anchor: in reality, it is a great glad tiding given in precarious circumstances.
